subject: MAP kickoff — security staffing & data custody for AcmeHealth evaluation
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — security staffing & data custody for AcmeHealth evaluation

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for the time on the product walkthrough last week. As discussed, we want to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align owners, milestones, and evidence lanes for the evaluation. Goal here is to make the SOC 2 evidence collection and data handling review as frictionless as possible so your security and procurement teams can complete their checks before your Oct 15 go/no-go.

Quick ask: can you confirm the primary contacts for the three lanes below (name + email) so we can fill the MAP:
- GRC / security review owner (sync with Redwood on control mapping and evidence inventory)
- SOC 2 evidence owner (responsible for pulling docs / attestations on your side)
- Data handling / Egress & PII/PHI point of contact (capturing acceptable handling, retention, and any required isolation)

Attached is a draft MAP and an evidence-roster template (MAP-AcmeHealth-v0.1.xlsx, evidence-roster-template.csv). I uploaded the same files to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/AcmeHealth/MAP-AcmeHealth-v0.1

Proposed timeline (flexible, but helps set expectations):
- By Aug 20: confirm owners and return the evidence-roster template with any pre-populated items
- Aug 23–Sep 10: evidence collection and technical Q&A (short tech syncs as needed)
- Sep 13–24: review of outstanding items, remediation plan if needed
- Oct 1–12: procurement & legal finalization, DocuSign if needed

If that timeline works, I’ll lock in a recurring 30-minute cadence (biweekly) and schedule focused tech sessions only when we need them. For the technical deep-dive I’ll bring Marissa (infrastructure lead) and for security fins we’ll loop in Vivek.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the MAP in motion.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP-AcmeHealth-v0.1.xlsx, evidence-roster-template.csv

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — security staffing & data custody for AcmeHealth evaluation

Thanks Sofia — happy to kick this off. Confirming our initial roster below:
- GRC / security review owner: Ben Ortiz (ben.ortiz@acmehealth.com) — IT Risk
- SOC 2 evidence owner: Claire D'Souza (contracts@acmehealth.com) — Legal (she coordinates evidence with ops)
- Data handling / PII owner: Alice Morgan (alice.morgan@acmehealth.com) — Data Governance

High-level notes from our side:
- We do encrypt at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Our default retention for analytics telemetry is 90 days; PHI/clinical traces have special handling and are kept in a segregated namespace. We will flag any items that must remain in our controlled environment and note them in the evidence roster.
- I’ve attached a simple data flow diagram to help Marissa and Vivek orient on where Redwood would sit in the path.

We can meet for a technical sync next Wednesday afternoon (Aug 18). I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

Cheers,

Alice Morgan
Head of Data Governance | Acme Health
alice.morgan@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — security staffing & data custody for AcmeHealth evaluation

Thanks Alice / Sofia. A couple of quick clarifying items from the Redwood security side before the tech sync: 
1) Can you confirm whether the segregated namespace for PHI is on a separate VPC/subnet or logical partitioning only? If there’s a separate VPC, we’ll note the network boundary in our control map.
2) For audit logs: what is the expected retention period you require for access logs (CloudTrail-type) vs application telemetry? Our hosted API keeps request metadata for 30 days by default but we can extend for an SLA agreement.
3) Any regulatory flags we should be aware of beyond HIPAA (e.g., regional data residency, state-level requirements)?

I’ve pasted Alice’s note below for quick reference. Let’s cover these items in the sync — if you can pre-populate the evidence roster with the current retention numbers that will speed things up.

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 11:34 AM Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sofia — happy to kick this off. Confirming our initial roster below:
> - GRC / security review owner: Ben Ortiz (ben.ortiz@acmehealth.com) — IT Risk

> - Data handling / PII owner: Alice Morgan (alice.morgan@acmehealth.com) — Data Governance

Thanks — I’ll bring the default retention/export options we support and a short checklist of what we can bundle into the evidence export.

Vivek
VP, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Hi all — looping in procurement details to help keep timelines aligned. Our procurement team requires the following to move to PO/contract signature:
- Completed MAP with evidence lanes assigned (we’ll review the evidence-roster CSV)
- Standard SLA exceptions documented and any indemnity clarifications called out
- DocuSign-ready contract (we aim to complete legal review by Sep 22 so Procures can issue a PO by Oct 1)

I opened a procurement checklist (attached) that maps our internal milestones to your proposed timeline — there are a couple of items where we typically ask for a 5–7 business day review cycle. I’ll circulate redlines early if anything deviates from our standard terms so we can try to keep to the Oct 1 PO target.
